Alex — thanks, great questions. Looping in David (infra/product engineer) and Neha (solutions/security lead) to address the technical bits.

Recap & proposed approach (high-level):

1) Supported auth modes and recommended patterns
   - API Keys (simple, great for server-to-server calls for non-sensitive workloads).
   - Service Accounts + JWT/OAuth2 (recommended for production access to protected datasets / regulated flows). Short-lived tokens issued to service accounts provide better control and rotation.
   - Hybrid: use long-lived API key scoped to a project for developer onboarding + short-lived service-account tokens for production-critical routes.

2) Rotation & TTL
   - Recommend quarterly rotation for long-lived keys; rotate earlier if suspicious activity.
   - Best practice: create new key, deploy consumers to accept new key, then revoke old key (zero-downtime with dual-accept mode).

3) KMS / HSM integration & audit logs
   - Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for encrypting secrets at rest and has audit logs for key usage in the Console. David will share specifics.

4) SDK snippets & header formats
   - We'll send sample SDK code and a short integration guide (attached).

Next steps:
  - David: technical write-up on token flows + key rotation recommendations (this week).
  - Neha: a quick note on compliance/KMS options for FinTechCo.
  - Schedule a 60-min integration workshop with your infra/security to walk through our SDK and token exchange flow.

Hi Alex — thanks for the great questions. Below is a pragmatic recommendation based on how most production customers (payments/fintech) integrate with Redwood.

Short summary (recommended):
- Use service accounts + short-lived JWT/OAuth tokens for all sensitive production traffic (user PII, transactions, or anything requiring auditability).
- Use scoped API keys for internal tooling, dev/test, and low-risk background jobs.

Details / patterns:
1) Service accounts + token exchange   
- Create a FinTechCo-managed service account in the Redwood Console. Assign minimal scopes (generate, embeddings:read, inference:write) per route.
- Exchange: FinTechCo signs a JWT using its private key and hits the Redwood token endpoint (/v1/token) to mint a short-lived Bearer token (15 minutes - configurable).
- Example request header for inference calls: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>

2) API keys & scoped usage
- Long-lived API key format for our example: rp_live_xxx (treat as secret).
- Support for key scoping: you can create keys with limited scope and IP restrictions.

3) Rotation & zero-downtime approach
- Create replacement key/service-account, configure consumers to accept both old+new (dual-accept) for a rollout window, then revoke the old key.
- For service accounts, keep a key-rotation job or use short TTL tokens to avoid long-lived private keys.

4) KMS / HSM / audit logging
- Redwood supports customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) to encrypt secrets at rest and integrates with our audit logs for key issuance and token exchanges. Audit entries include src IP, principal, route, and token_kid.

5) JWKS & signature validation
- If FinTechCo will validate tokens, we publish a JWKS endpoint: https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json. Tokens include 'kid' and are RS256-signed.

6) Embeddings / rerankers considerations
- Calls that create / use embeddings are subject to the same auth model. We recommend service-account tokens for production embedding pipelines. For reranking endpoints used in real-time, use short-lived Bearer tokens.

Sample curl (token exchange + inference call):
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"assertion":"<signed_jwt>", "grant_type":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer"}'

# then
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <minted_token>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"input":"summarize..."}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference/model-id

Attachments: redwood-api-key-rotation-recommendation.pdf (detailed rotation checklist)

I'll join the integration workshop to walk through live token exchanges and help sketch sample code for your infra team.
